title: Development and Production Modes
keywords: Vue Project Structure and Application Basics
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of Development and Production Modes in a Vue 3 application.
Apply at least one of the syllabus subtopics in a small, inspectable example.
Verify one expected behavior and identify a relevant edge case.

content.intro: This lesson studies Development and Production Modes within Vue Project Structure and Application Basics. The source PDF subtopics are preserved below and connected to an original working-style example.
content.why_it_matters: Understanding the project skeleton makes it easier to find the right file and diagnose setup or build errors instead of changing unrelated parts.

content_blocks.title: The idea in context
content_blocks.text: A Vue project combines Single-File Components, an application entry point, Vite tooling, assets, and package configuration. This lesson focuses on Development and Production Modes. Start by naming the state, component, browser behavior, or deployment boundary involved; then predict what should change and test the smallest example.

items.title: Running the development server
items.text: For Running the development server, connect the term to a visible behavior in a small Vue 3 example. State what input or reactive dependency changes, predict the UI result, and verify the prediction with a normal case plus a boundary case.

items.title: Hot Module Replacement
items.text: For Hot Module Replacement, trace the path from the entry point to the root component, then identify the configuration or tool responsible for compiling and serving it. Use the official create-vue/Vite workflow for a fresh Vue 3 project and keep dependency versions reproducible.

items.title: Creating a production build
items.text: For Creating a production build, decide which code runs during build, on the server, and in the browser. Keep output deterministic during hydration, isolate state per server request, keep secrets server-only, and test the actual production build rather than relying only on the dev server.

content_blocks.code:
npm run build
npm run preview
content_blocks.expected_output: Vite writes production files to dist/ and serves a local preview of those built files.
content_blocks.run_instructions: Run from the Vue project root after npm install; inspect the generated dist/ assets and do not commit temporary output unless your project requires it.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the initial values or original code, reload the development app/test, and repeat once with a boundary or failure case. Remove temporary logs and test data before committing.

content_blocks.title: Guided example
content_blocks.text: Work through Development and Production Modes with a predict–change–verify loop. First state the expected UI or console output. Change only the relevant input/state value, then observe the result. Compare it with the expected output in the code block; if it differs, check the exact file, runtime/version, browser Console, and network response before widening the investigation.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Extend the example to include “Hot Module Replacement”. Keep the same behavior for the ordinary input, then try an empty, invalid, repeated, or failure condition that makes sense for the example. Record the expected result before testing.

items.title: Assuming behavior instead of checking it
items.text: Write down the expected result and reproduce the issue in the smallest possible example; inspect the browser Console and the exact reactive value or request.

items.title: Ignoring an edge case
items.text: Try empty input, a missing item, repeated interaction, a failed request, or unmounting while work is pending; handle the case explicitly.

items.title: Putting every responsibility in one component
items.text: Separate display, reusable logic, API service, and shared state when that boundary makes the behavior easier to test and explain.

content_blocks.title: Recap
content_blocks.text: Remember: A Vue project combines Single-File Components, an application entry point, Vite tooling, assets, and package configuration. For Development and Production Modes, keep the example small, verify the rendered or logged result, and consult the official references when behavior depends on a specific Vue or ecosystem version.

content_blocks.title: Accessibility, version, and runtime notes
content_blocks.text: Use semantic HTML, readable labels, keyboard-operable controls, and visible errors where the example interacts with users. Vue examples are intended for Vue 3.x with create-vue/Vite unless a legacy or specialist lesson explicitly says otherwise. This CodeLeaf playground does not execute arbitrary Vue code; the snippets are labeled for static validation and should be run in a separate local project.

content.task: Create a small example for “Development and Production Modes” that applies “Running the development server”, predicts the expected result, and verifies a relevant boundary case.
task_acceptance_criteria: The example demonstrates the named Vue concept rather than only mentioning it.
The expected output or observable behavior is written down and can be checked locally.
At least one boundary, loading, invalid-input, or failure case is tested or explicitly reasoned about.
The example uses semantic/accessible interaction patterns and does not treat frontend state as authoritative security.
hints: Start with the smallest observable part of “Running the development server”.
Predict the output before changing one input at a time.
Use the browser Console, Vue DevTools, or the appropriate test runner to isolate a mismatch.

common_mistakes.problem: The example only covers the happy path.
common_mistakes.why: Real interfaces receive empty values, delayed responses, invalid input, and failed requests.
common_mistakes.fix: Add one realistic edge/failure case and state its expected behavior.

common_mistakes.problem: The code assumes an API or feature exists in every runtime.
common_mistakes.why: Tool and API support depends on Vue, the build tool, or the chosen SSR/test framework.
common_mistakes.fix: Check the linked official reference and record the runtime/version assumption.

summary: Development and Production Modes belongs to the broader area Vue Project Structure and Application Basics.
The main concept to practice is Running the development server.
Verify a normal result and one meaningful boundary case before using the pattern in a production feature.
